machine.dedicated_or_shared: SHARED — same cloud sandbox used for H3/H4/H5/H6, not dedicated benchmarking hardware. Classified LIMITED/PILOT for this reason per Stage 13's standing instruction for this environment.

runtime_build_track.note: This experiment is a client-side comparison only (server is a fixed, non-runtime Python implementation — see 'server_configuration'). Release builds used for all three client runtimes, as specified by the H2 kickoff instruction itself (Section 8: 'Primary track: Release builds, consistent across all three runtimes... Do not imply this experiment uses source-controlled builds').

deno.install_method: release binary, downloaded from denoland/deno GitHub Releases in an earlier stage of this session

server_configuration.implementation: Python 3 stdlib http.server (ThreadingHTTPServer + BaseHTTPRequestHandler), NOT implemented in any of the three tested runtimes — this is deliberate, per Stage 12 Section 14's rule that the client must never become a hidden variable by also swapping the server implementation.
server_configuration.bind_address: 127.0.0.1 (IPv4 explicit — no DNS, no dual-stack ambiguity)

routes./: fixed 11-byte JSON body {"ok":true}, default HTTP/1.1 persistent connection (keep-alive) — used for the KEEP-ALIVE phase
routes./cold: identical body, but server sends `Connection: close`, forcing the client to close and re-establish a fresh TCP connection for its next request (standard HTTP/1.1 protocol semantics, not a client-side hack) — used for the COLD phase
routes./stats: returns live connection/request counters for verification; querying it itself opens one connection but does not increment the request counters

server_configuration.tcp_nodelay: Explicitly set on every accepted server socket (socket.IPPROTO_TCP / TCP_NODELAY). DISCLOSED FIX: smoke-testing before the official run found latencies with large (tens-of-ms), alternating spikes consistent with a classic Nagle's-algorithm/delayed-ACK interaction on small HTTP request/response packets. Setting TCP_NODELAY on the server socket (a setting applied identically for all three client comparisons, since it's server-side) resolved the large spikes for Bun and Deno; see 'client_warmup_methodology' for the remaining Node-specific finding.
server_configuration.single_server_instance: One server process was started once and used for the smoke test plus the entire cold and keep-alive phases for all three runtimes — literally the same running process, not just the same implementation, satisfying the 'identical server for every client comparison' requirement as strictly as possible.

client_warmup_methodology.finding: A fixed, small, equal warmup count across runtimes was NOT sufficient. Smoke-testing (after fixing TCP_NODELAY) found Node's fetch (undici) needed roughly 8,000-16,000 warmup requests on a persistent connection before its per-request keep-alive latency stabilized — Bun stabilized around 2,000-4,000, Deno around 4,000-8,000. Using a small equal warmup budget would have made Node look far slower than its true steady-state behavior, for a warmup-insufficiency reason unrelated to M9.
client_warmup_methodology.fix: Keep-alive mode uses a chunked, predefined warmup-stability check (same style as H5's), extended (bounded, up to 128,000 iterations) until stable, REQUIRING TWO CONSECUTIVE PASSING ATTEMPTS (not just one) before declaring STABLE — a single-attempt check was found to be fooled by an intermediate JIT-tiering plateau in Node's fetch specifically (looked flat around 1,000-4,000 iterations at an elevated latency, but kept improving further). This design was finalized BEFORE the official 10-run data collection for each runtime and was not modified afterward. The exact warmup iteration count used is recorded per run (see raw data) and varied naturally by runtime as a result of this process (Bun: 2,000-4,000; Deno: 4,000-8,000; Node: 16,000-32,000) — not tuned to favor any runtime.
client_warmup_methodology.cold_mode_warmup: A SEPARATE, fixed 300-request warmup (no stability-seeking loop) is used for cold mode. DISCLOSED FIX: applying the same escalating stability-check algorithm to cold mode during smoke-testing caused runaway warmup (one run reached thousands of connections before the smoke test was stopped), because cold connection-establishment overhead is inherently noisy on every single request (that's the definition of 'cold') and does not converge to a tight steady state the way a persistent-connection measurement does. This is a design distinction (connection warmup does not apply to cold mode by definition — only JIT/process warmup does, which converges much faster), decided before the official run based on this smoke-test finding, not tuned afterward to produce a particular result.

background_workload.description: Shared cloud sandbox; server, client, and orchestrator all run on the SAME 2-core machine (loopback only) — the same limitation documented for H4/H6. Session-management processes present as in prior experiments.
background_workload.load_generator_placement: N/A — no separate load-generator tool was used; the client script itself issues sequential (concurrency=1) requests and times them directly via process.hrtime.bigint(), which is the cleanest available isolation of per-request dispatch overhead per Section 14.

cpu_monitoring.method: psutil 7.2.2, server-process cpu_percent() sampled once per client-process run (before/after, not continuously sampled mid-run) via cpu_percent(interval=None) primed before the run and read after.
cpu_monitoring.results_summary: Server CPU% stayed well below saturation in every combo (max observed: ~68.6% for a bun-cold run; node-keepalive ~40%; see summary.json per_combo_summary[*].server_cpu_percent_during_run). This is consistent with the server never becoming the bottleneck — server load tracked client request rate (higher for faster clients, lower for Node, exactly as expected if the CLIENT is the pacing factor), not an independent confound.

runs.smoke_test: 5 keep-alive + 5 cold requests per runtime, run first; verified status 200, exact body match, exact Content-Length match, and connection-reuse behavior (keep-alive: <5 connections opened; cold: connections opened within 2%% of expected warmup+timed request count) for all three runtimes before proceeding. PASSED for all three on the first attempt after the TCP_NODELAY and warmup-methodology fixes described above.
